title: Unified Model Rollouts (Canary & A/B) — PRD, Design, Roadmap, Pricing & Release Notes
author: Maya Patel
content:
Summary
-------
This document consolidates the product overview, PRD (requirements), design specifications, roadmap, pricing guidance, and release notes for the Unified Model Rollouts feature (canary and A/B rollouts). The feature enables safe, observable, and policy-driven model rollouts across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

Goals
-----
- Provide first-class API and Console support for model rollouts (canary, A/B, phased ramp) with minimal application changes.
- Make rollouts observable and reversible: per-route traffic split, metric-based automatic rollback, and clear audit logs.
- Support cross-environment rollouts: Hosted API, Dedicated, Private (VPC).
- Reduce human effort and incident risk during model version changes.

Non-goals
---------
- Full CI/CD model training pipelines (out of scope).
- Multi-tenant sharing of rollout configs across customers (each customer has independent rollouts).

Background and Motivation
-------------------------
Customers often need to migrate traffic between model versions for quality/regression testing, cost experiments (quantized vs full), or hardware tiering. Current options are manual (change model_id per-route) and lack safe ramp controls, automatic rollback, or clear auditability. This causes quality regressions in production and operational toil.

User Personas
------------
- Product/Feature Engineers: set up canaries to validate model quality on a subset of traffic.
- ML Engineers: run A/B experiments to measure metric deltas (e.g., hallucination rate, response quality).
- Platform/DevOps: enforce rollout policies, monitor SLOs and costs.

User Stories
------------
1. As an ML engineer, I want to route 5% of traffic to a new model variant for 48 hours and automatically ramp to 100% if quality metrics remain within thresholds.
2. As a product engineer, I want to run an A/B test comparing Redwood-quantized-v2 against baseline and record per-variant metrics for analysis.
3. As a platform engineer, I want rollouts to be auditable and to support rollback within 1 minute of a failed threshold.

Requirements (PRD)
------------------
Must have:
- API to create/update/delete Rollout objects with: name, target_routes, variant_list (model_id, weight, metadata), start_time, duration, ramp_policy, stop_conditions (metric thresholds), owner, and tags.
- Console UI to visualize traffic splits, per-variant metrics (latency, token_count, cost, custom eval metrics), and audit trail for changes.
- Automatic rollback when monitored metrics breach thresholds for a configurable window.
- Support for percent-based and absolute traffic controls.
- Permissioning: RBAC integration (only users with rollout:create can create; rollout:approve required for cross-env rollouts).

Should have:
- Integrations with Redwood Optimize to suggest ramp schedules and quantization-aware variants.
- Canary request sampling options (random, cookie-based sticky, header-injected).
- SDK hooks and examples for client-side opt-in/opt-out.

Nice to have:
- Built-in experiment analysis and champion/challenger selection.
- Policy templates for regulated customers (finance/health).

Success Metrics
---------------
- Adoption: 30% of model version changes use Rollouts within 6 months of GA.
- Safety: < 3% of rollouts require manual rollback after auto-rollback enabled.
- Time to detect & rollback: median detection+rollback time < 90s for configured thresholds.
- Operational cost impact: customers should be able to estimate per-rollout cost delta in Console.

API Contract (example)
---------------------
POST /v1/rollouts
Request body (JSON):
{
  "name": "canary-quantized-v2-2026-03",
  "target_routes": ["/v1/generate-chat"],
  "variants": [
    {"model_id": "redwood/ggml-v1", "weight": 95, "metadata": {"quant": "int8"}},
    {"model_id": "redwood/ggml-v2-quant", "weight": 5, "metadata": {"note": "canary"}}
  ],
  "ramp_policy": {"type": "linear", "steps": [{"after_min_minutes": 60, "target_weight": 20}, {"after_min_minutes": 240, "target_weight": 100}]},
  "stop_conditions": [{"metric": "error_rate", "operator": ">", "threshold": "0.02", "window_seconds": 600}],
  "owner": "team-ml",
  "tags": ["canary","quantization"]
}

Design Overview
---------------
Architecture components:
- Rollout Controller Service (RCS): central coordinator for schedule evaluation, ramping, and executing traffic changes.
- Traffic Router: high-throughput component (co-located with serving runtime) that applies per-route traffic split decisions, supports sticky sessions, and emits detailed telemetry.
- Metrics Engine: aggregates per-variant metrics (latency histograms, token counts, custom eval signals) with time-series storage and rule evaluation.
- Audit & Policy Service: stores change history, enforces RBAC, and stores rollback templates.

Data flow:
1. User creates Rollout via API or Console.
2. RCS validates policy, stores rollout state, and schedules ramp events.
3. RCS sends signed, versioned traffic rules to Traffic Router(s).
4. Traffic Routers apply split and emit per-variant metrics to Metrics Engine.
5. Metrics Engine evaluates stop_conditions and notifies RCS to trigger rollback if needed.

Design constraints & SLOs:
- RCS API availability: 99.95% (monthly).
- Time-to-propagate (RCS -> all Traffic Routers within same region): P95 < 15s.
- Traffic Router per-request latency overhead: < 2ms P95 added to baseline.
- Metrics ingestion latency: P50 < 10s, P95 < 30s for rollout metrics.

Traffic Rule Format (YAML example)
--------------------------------
- name: canary-quantized-v2-2026-03
  routes:
    - path: /v1/generate-chat
  variants:
    - id: redwood/ggml-v2-quant
      weight: 5
      sticky: true
    - id: redwood/ggml-v1
      weight: 95
  ramp_policy:
    type: linear
    steps:
      - after_min_minutes: 60
        target_weight: 20
      - after_min_minutes: 240
        target_weight: 100
  stop_conditions:
    - metric: error_rate
      operator: ">"
      threshold: "0.02"
      window_seconds: 600

Console UX Notes
----------------
- Rollout list page: filter/sort by status, owner, tags. Quick actions: pause, resume, rollback, duplicate.
- Rollout detail page: timeline visualization of weight changes, per-variant charts (latency, cost, custom metrics), audit trail (who changed what and when).
- One-click promote to 100% when metrics are green.

Security & Compliance
--------------------
- All rollout changes are recorded in audit log with user, IP, and SAML context.
- RBAC enforced via existing AuthN/AuthZ service: rollout:create, rollout:approve, rollout:modify, rollout:delete.
- For Private deployments, rollout controller can run in customer-managed control plane; signed rule bundles are used to prevent tampering.

Roadmap & Themes (Q1 2026 - Q4 2026)
------------------------------------
- Q1 2026 (Alpha): API + basic Traffic Router support (percent splits), Console read-only visualization, manual ramping. Target: private preview customers.
- Q2 2026 (Beta): Ramp policies, stop conditions, automatic rollback, RBAC integration, metrics UI. Target: wider beta customers (hosted + dedicated).
- Q3 2026 (GA): Cross-environment rollouts, sticky routing options, SDK examples, Optimize integration for ramp suggestions. GA for Hosted and Dedicated.
- Q4 2026 (Enterprise): Audit templates, regulated policy bundles, advanced experiment analytics, pricing/packaging launch.

Pricing & Packaging Notes
------------------------
Pricing goals:
- Align with Redwood’s usage-based model but reflect operational value of rollouts and increased metric ingestion/retention costs.

Proposed packaging:
- Included (Free tier): Basic rollouts (manual create, up to 1 active rollout, 7-day retention of rollout metrics).
- Core (standard hosted usage): Up to 5 concurrent active rollouts, automated ramping & rollbacks, 30-day retention. Pricing: add-on +$250/month per tenant or bundled for Pro customers.
- Enterprise (Dedicated/Private): Unlimited rollouts, longer retention (90+ days), SAML/SCIM RBAC integration, on-prem controller deployment support. Pricing: included in Dedicated reserved capacity contracts or negotiated enterprise license.

Per-rollout metric ingestion surcharge:
- A lightweight surcharge on metrics for rollouts that create >1M per-variant metric samples/day. Example: $0.001 per extra sample-equivalent above threshold (billing blended into monitoring usage).

Release Notes: v1.0 (GA) — 2026-09-15
--------------------------------
Features shipped:
- Rollout API (create/update/delete) with JSON contract shown above.
- Console rollout pages: create wizard (beta), timeline, per-variant metrics, and quick rollback.
- Traffic Router changes to support per-route percent splits and sticky routing.
- Automatic rollback based on single metric rules (error_rate, latency_p95).
- Audit logging and RBAC hooks.
Known limitations:
- Experiment analysis is manual (CSV export).
- Private deployments require additional on-prem controller packaging for GA (coming Q4).

Rollout Runbook (Operational steps)
----------------------------------
1. Pre-rollout checks:
   - Verify baseline metrics for target routes (latency, error_rate, token cost).
   - Announce planned rollout window to stakeholders.
2. Create rollout with conservative initial weight (<=5%).
3. Monitor metrics dashboard for 2x configured window; if metrics stable, proceed to next ramp step.
4. If stop_conditions triggered: RCS will auto-rollback. If manual rollback required: use Console > Rollout > Rollback (1-click) and contact oncall@redwood.com.
5. Post-rollback: open postmortem if incident severity >= Sev 2.

Operational Ownership
---------------------
- Product/Feature: Maya Patel (owner).
- Runtime/Traffic Router: Eng-serving-runtime team (owner: Daniel Kim).
- Metrics & Alerting: Eng-platform (owner: Arjun Mehta).
- SRE oncall: Eng-sre rotation for incidents.

Open Questions / Decisions
-------------------------
- Decision: default auto-rollback window will be 10 minutes (TBD by security/compliance).
- Question: should per-variant cost estimates be shown pre-rollout? (UX + billing integration needed).
